summary: Recent M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY. Robotics and computer vision work spanning multi-sensor integration across cameras, ToF, and accelerometers, and 3D geometry including homography estimation, DH-based kinematic chains, and monocular depth reconstruction. Implements and optimizes algorithms in C++ and Python on ROS 2 and Ubuntu.

experience.title: Research Intern (Capstone)
bullets: Architected a metal surface inspection pipeline in Python and OpenCV combining custom image stitching, wavelet denoising, and monocular depth estimation for microscopic crack analysis.
Designed a custom wavelet bank (sym6+bior3.5) and optimized homography-based stitching with concurrency, raising reconstruction quality from PSNR 65 to PSNR 86 over the baseline.
Deployed ZoeDepth monocular depth estimation for crack-depth profiling, achieving +/-8% error on 3D surface reconstruction.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove translating 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands, integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with a Raspberry Pi over Bluetooth in Python.
Calibrated accelerometer output in software, resolving sensor jitter through a z-axis differential thresholding algorithm and resolution tuning to stabilize tap detection.

projects.name: ROS 2 Robotic Arm Kinematics (UR5e & AL5B)
bullets: Derived DH parameter tables and hand-computed full forward kinematic chains (0T6) for a 6-DoF UR5e and a 5-DoF AL5B, validating the transforms against MoveIt and RViz URDF models in ROS 2 Humble and ROS Noetic.
Planned and executed collision-free pick-and-place trajectories on the physical UR5e via the UR ROS 2 driver; AL5B repeatability measured at under 2 mm over 10 trials.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled, Vision-Guided Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - M.S. Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built a multi-sensor pick-and-place system mapping image-space YOLO detections to arm workspace coordinates, range-gated by dual VL53L0X ToF sensors on a TCA9548A I2C mux; 100% pick reliability over 10 trials.
Implemented two-link inverse kinematics in C++ on the arm controller and deployed a TensorRT-optimized YOLO detector on Jetson for visual servoing, cutting inference from 56.7 ms to 10.9 ms (5.2x).

projects.name: Autonomous Driving Perception Stack in CARLA
bullets: Built automated data generation pipelines using CARLA semantic segmentation and raycast occlusion filtering to produce ~5,000 YOLO and ~3,000 lane-detection training frames with zero manual annotation.
Trained YOLO11n (mAP50 ~0.85) and fine-tuned UFLD lane detection (ResNet-18); integrated into an adaptive control stack validated in Town02 at zero collisions.

awards: 1st Prize, Poster Presentation - 2D and 3D Image Mosaicing of Microscopic Images, F.C.R.I.T. (2024)
